//Jwt: Jwt:Key is empty on purpose: a token signing key must never be committed. Supply the real key through the host's secret store, i.e. the Jwt__Key environment variable. Generate it with: dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:Key" "$(openssl rand -base64 48)" locally, or a fresh 64-char random string in production. The API refuses to start without it.
//ConnectionStrings: This default carries no credential. VerichatDB authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID only, so the string names a server and a directory identity and holds no password to leak. Active Directory Default resolves a managed identity first, which is what the Azure App Service copy of the API presents once Identity -> System assigned is On and Database/azure-managed-identity-user.sql has run; on a developer machine it falls through to the signed-in IDE credential. Monster ASP can do neither, which is why it no longer hosts an API that reads this database. Program.cs refuses to start when this key is missing, and refuses to start outside Development if the string asks for Encrypt=False. Local development is unchanged: appsettings.Development.json keeps LocalDB, but a stale dotnet user-secrets entry outranks that file and would silently send a local run somewhere else. See DEPLOYMENT.md 7.4.
//Cors: Origins allowed to call this API from a browser with credentials. The staff web app is deployed to a different runasp.net site, so its origin must be listed here or the SignalR hub and every fetch() from notifications.js fails. Deployed origins are not secret, so they live in this file; extra environments go in the Cors__AllowedOrigins__2 environment variable.
//Bootstrap: The application creates NO demo business data. The first System Administrator is created once, only when the user table is completely empty, from these values. Leave AdminEmail/AdminPassword/AdminName blank here and supply real values as environment variables (Bootstrap__AdminEmail / Bootstrap__AdminPassword / Bootstrap__AdminName) so no credential is committed to source control. Change the password and delete the variables after first sign-in. DemoUsers is on in this file because this project is submitted for assessment and the marker signs in from the deployed site: it makes startup write one account per role, and the web tier reads the same key to render the one-click buttons. That is a deliberate exposure - the seven passwords are in README.md, so ANYONE who can reach this host can open any role including the administrator. A deployment holding real client data must set Bootstrap__DemoUsers=false (or remove the key), and the account set should be deleted from the Users table.
//Email: SMTP for the two notices this system sends by itself: an email-confirmation link and a password-reset link. Every value is blank here and comes from the host's secret store (Email__Host / Email__Port / Email__UseSsl / Email__Username / Email__Password / Email__FromAddress / Email__FromName) so no mail credential is committed. While Email__Host is empty each message is logged instead of sent - the development case, and also the fail-safe: an email token or a new password is recorded whether or not the mail server answers.
//Sites: The origin the emailed links are built against. Reset and confirmation pages belong to the web app rather than to this API - a form served from the API would have nowhere to post back to - so the link uses the web site's origin. Deployed origins are not secret and are already listed in Cors. Run the web app somewhere else and override it with Sites__WebBaseUrl, e.g. http://localhost:5253.
